ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure containing R1 and R2 substituents, with several curved arrows present; according to the problem statement, ignore these arrows and look only at the atomic connectivity. It can be seen that the left-end R1 is connected to a chain composed of four unlabeled skeleton carbons, and the right end of the chain is connected to a positively charged nitrogen; this nitrogen is also connected to hydrogen and R2. Reasoning: Represent both R1 and R2 with wildcard atoms *; write the four unlabeled skeleton carbons in sequence as CCCC; according to the specified method, write the positively charged nitrogen connected to the carbon chain and the second wildcard atom as [NH2+]*. Combining in the order of connectivity gives *CCCC[NH2+]*.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a connectivity graph rather than a mechanism: R1—C—C—C—C—N(+)(H)—R2, ignoring all curved arrows. Replace R1 and R2 with wildcard atoms `*`. Convert the four unlabeled skeletal atoms between R1 and N into `CCCC`. Encode the charged nitrogen attached to the chain and the second wildcard as `[NH2+]*`. Combine these in order to obtain `*CCCC[NH2+]*`.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the chemical drawing while ignoring the curved arrows: the left endpoint is an R1 substituent attached to a carbon chain; the skeleton contains four consecutive aliphatic carbon atoms leading to a positively charged nitrogen. The nitrogen is bonded to the carbon chain, to H, and to R2, and is marked with a positive charge.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction that asks for the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and explicitly says to ignore the arrows.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: unspecified R groups can be represented by wildcard atoms `*`; skeletal line vertices without labels are carbons; a protonated/positively charged amine nitrogen with two hydrogens and two single bonds is written as `[NH2+]`; curved arrows are not atoms or bonds and must be omitted.
